stem: A child with asthma is prescribed prednisolone for an acute exacerbation. Which statement best describes prednisolone?

options.text: A short-course oral corticosteroid used to reduce airway inflammation
A short-acting beta2 agonist used for immediate bronchodilation
An inhaled corticosteroid used as maintenance therapy
A leukotriene receptor antagonist used for symptom prevention

explanation: Prednisolone is an oral corticosteroid commonly used in acute asthma exacerbations to reduce airway inflammation. It is not a bronchodilator and is not the usual maintenance controller medication.
rationale: The original item was a fill-in-the-blank about prednisolone rather than a single-best-answer question, so it was rewritten to test the same core concept in SBA format.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: prednisolone is an oral corticosteroid given as a short course in acute asthma.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect: short-acting beta2 agonists are relievers such as salbutamol.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect: inhaled corticosteroids are controller medications, not prednisolone.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect: leukotriene receptor antagonists are preventive controllers, not oral steroids.
